system.description:
Less about the one perfect tool, more about the shelf of forty imperfect ones. Something in the bag always does the job. Taught among the guild alchemists who sell potions on the open market, and the Ysoki Society's tonic-brewers under Nhool Sizzlefang.

  • Brew Formula (1st): During a long rest, brew formulas from your known list. Each costs 1 Ingenuity Point (2 for a damaging one) and keeps until used. You can hold brewed formulas equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Artificer level; extras go inert.
  • Efficient Brewing (3rd): Formulas cost 1 less Ingenuity Point to brew (minimum 1).
  • Combat Alchemy (5th): Brew a single formula on the spot as an action at double the normal Ingenuity cost.
  • Volatile Mastery (7th): Your bombs and harmful formulas deal an additional die of damage.
  • Lasting Work: Perfected Formula (10th): As often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and materials (see Lasting Work) to perfect one formula into a permanent-effect item (a ring that continuously radiates Draught of Clarity's protection, a self-refilling flask of Elixir of Vigour, or a blade permanently coated with Caustic Flask's acid) rather than a consumable.
  • Great Work (24th): The Panacea: brew a legendary elixir capable of curing any one affliction, condition, or injury when drunk, including things no ordinary Restoration-tier magic touches. One dose a year. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and materials as for Lasting Work.

Known Formulas

  • Fire Bomb — Thrown — 2d6 fire damage, plus 1d6 per five Artificer levels, in a 10ft radius, Reflex save for half
  • Elixir of Vigour — Drink to gain temporary HP equal to 1d8 + Intelligence modifier
  • Caustic Flask — Thrown, 20ft: the target makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC or takes 1d6 acid damage a round for 3 rounds
  • Draught of Clarity — Drink for Advantage on your next saving throw vs a mind-affecting effect within 1 hour
  • Smoke Powder Bomb — Thrown, 20ft: as the Gadgeteer's Smoke Bomb
  • Sovereign Glue — Bonds two objects together permanently, or until dissolved by a specific solvent
  • Universal Solvent — A few drops dissolve any adhesive on contact, including your own Sovereign Glue (the Catalogue's Slippery Oil does the same)
  • Draught of Steady Hands — Drink for Advantage on your next Dexterity-based check within 1 hour
  • Numbing Salve — Applied to a wound: the recipient ignores the effects of one level of Exhaustion for 1 hour
  • Choking Gas Vial — Thrown, 20ft: a 10ft radius; creatures make a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC or can't speak or cast verbal spells for 1 round
  • Quickfoam — Thrown at a fire or flammable area — extinguishes flames in a 10ft radius instantly
  • Reagent of Revealing — A few drops on a surface reveal invisible writing, residue, or a recently-handled object's last handler (GM discretion)

Designing a Custom Formula

  • Benchmark: A thrown or drunk formula should land at roughly a 1st-level spell's potency — 2d6 damage in a small area, a single round of a save-or-suffer condition, or a flat, narrow buff (Advantage on one specific roll type, or temporary HP equal to a small die plus Intelligence modifier).
  • Formulas that grant information or utility (detection, identification, minor restoration) should require a genuine cost — a rare ingredient, a full round to apply, or a limited number of uses — rather than being free and repeatable.
  • A custom option that deals damage scales as Fire Bomb does (+1d6 per five Artificer levels); otherwise it may grant Advantage on one roll.
  • No infusion, gadget or formula restores hit points.
